Whether DDCIs penetrate the central nervous system (CNS) in the context of potential blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction in PD and influence levodopa efficacy is unclear. We therefore assessed CNS exposure of benserazide (BZ) and its active metabolite 2,3,4-trihydroxybenzylhydrazine (THBH) and their association with levodopa response. Fifteen PD patients (Hoehn-Yahr 2-3) underwent a standardized levodopa challenge test and were classified as good (≥50% improvement) or poor responders. Paired blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples were collected after a single oral dose of levodopa/BZ (200/50 mg), and analyte concentrations were quantified using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography with electrochemical detection (UPLC-ECD). Both BZ and THBH were detectable in CSF, indicating BBB penetration. CSF concentrations and CSF-to-plasma ratios of total BZ (BZ + THBH) were significantly higher in poor responders (p = 0.021 and 0.014, respectively) and negatively correlated with levodopa efficacy (p = 0.034 and 0.008, respectively). In contrast, levodopa concentrations and QAlb did not differ between groups. These findings demonstrate CNS exposure of BZ/THBH and suggest that increased central DDCI exposure may contribute to reduced levodopa responsiveness.

title: Precision Prediction of Microbial Ecosystem Impact on Host Metabolism Using Genome-Resolved Metagenomics.
abstract: Mammalian gut dysbiosis is recognized to influence host metabolism, yet key microbiota and mechanisms governing their effects remain poorly understood. Here we developed a genome-resolved ecology-aware, systems-level workflow to predict how gut microbial metabolism affects mammalian health, and we apply it to a "spinal cord-gut axis" dataset. By scaling and integrating temporally resolved network analytics and consensus statistical approaches, we identified 19 microbial species that best predict host physiology following neurological impairment. In silico validation through pathway-centric and comparative genomic analyses revealed that among these species, the biggest encoded microbial metabolic changes were in pathways linked to host nitrogen balance, varying by host sex and microbial ecotype/species. Further inference identified the specific bacteria (and their draft genomes) potentially driving urease-dependent versus amino acid-dependent nitrogen metabolism-findings that can explain previously mechanistically-ambiguous, but clinically relevant, ammonia-driven host nitrogen imbalance. This provides a generalizable data-driven hypothesis generation workflow for longitudinal microbiome data.

title: Impact of concomitant benzodiazepine receptor agonist and antidepressant use on the incidence of postoperative delirium after head and neck tumor surgery.
abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) occurs after oncologic head and neck surgery with an incidence of 18,95%, and is with 25,43% even higher in patients with oral cancer. It also rises significantly with prolonged surgery duration > 6 h. Due to overlapping risk factors of POD and oral squamous cell carcinoma, patients undergoing head and neck cancer surgery are at increased risk for POD. The objective of our study was to evaluate the influence of a pre-existing concomitant medication with benzodiazepines receptor agonists (BZARs) or antidepressants on the risk for POD. This retrospective analysis was drawn with data from the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery of the University Hospital Erlangen. Included in the study were patients who underwent tumor resection and immediate microvascular reconstruction in between 2021 and 2024. The influence of BZARs and antidepressants on the incidence of POD was examined using logistic regression models. Age ≥ 70 was the only statistically significant risk factor (aOR 5.38, 95% CI: 2.18-13.30, p < 0.001). Concomitant medication with BZARs showed no relevant influence on POD intervals (aOR 2.11, 95% CI: 0.40-11.17, p = 0.38), in an unadjusted analysis an association between concomitant use of antidepressants and POD could be assumed, despite not reaching statistical significance in adjusted analysis (aOR 1.64, 95% CI 0.53-5.1, p = 0.39). The current body of evidence on the influence of BZARs on POD is highly heterogeneous in the literature and the overall level of evidence remains low. Concomitant BZAR use was not significantly associated with POD in the present study. Concomitant use of antidepressants was associated with POD in the univariable analysis, suggesting a potential clinical relevance; however, this association was not confirmed in the multivariable analysis. Age ≥ 70 is a significant risk factor for POD.

title: Characterization of blood metabolomic responses to deep brain stimulation in patients with Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) constitutes one of the few therapeutic strategies for advanced Parkinson's disease. Although DBS causes rapid alterations in neuronal metabolism, whether it remodels the circulating metabolome and thereby alleviates systemic symptoms remains unknown. Here, we used high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry to perform untargeted plasma metabolomics of plasma samples from patients with Parkinson's disease pre- and post-DBS to profile transient metabolic alterations in plasma that could be attributed to DBS. Numerous metabolites involved in tyrosine metabolism-including dopamine, phenylacetaldehyde, 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde, and tyrosine-were reduced in abundance following DBS. In contrast, metabolites such as lactate were increased in abundance in response to DBS. We further characterized metabolites associated with the immediate therapeutic effects of DBS and identified acrylic acid level as a potential metabolic predictor of long-term prognosis. Collectively, our findings provide important insights into DBS-induced reprogramming of the plasma metabolome.

title: Advance care planning and care coordination for people with parkinsonism: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Parkinsonism comprises a group of progressive neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson's disease and atypical parkinsonism. In advanced stages, advance care planning (ACP) and coordinated care are important to align treatment with patients' values and reduce unwanted interventions and caregiver burden. In this study we evaluated whether a nurse-led intervention increases documentation of end-of-life preferences and improves patient and caregiver outcomes. In this multicentre, single-blind randomized controlled trial (2020-2022), participants with parkinsonism (Hoehn & Yahr stage ≥3) and their caregivers were included across seven neurology centres in Austria, Estonia, Germany, Greece, Italy, Sweden, and the UK. Participants were randomized 1:1 to either the PD_Pal intervention (a structured six-month nurse-led ACP and care coordination program) or usual care. The primary outcome was documentation of end-of-life preferences at six months. A total of 189 people with parkinsonism and 189 family caregivers were enrolled. No significant difference was found in documentation of end-of-life preferences between groups (P = 0.77). Caregivers in the intervention group reported improved quality of life at six months (P = 0.03), although this effect was not sustained at 12 months. No differences were observed in other outcomes. These findings highlight challenges in implementing ACP in advanced parkinsonism and the need for flexible, stage-appropriate strategies.

title: Refractory ventricular tachyarrhythmia following a suicidal massive caffeine overdose: a case report and review of emergency management.
abstract: Caffeine is one of the most widely consumed psychoactive substances worldwide and is readily accessible in tablet formulations and caffeinated beverages. Although moderate caffeine intake is generally considered safe, massive acute ingestion can result in severe toxicity involving the central nervous and cardiovascular systems. Life-threatening manifestations include seizures, profound electrolyte disturbances, metabolic derangements, and malignant ventricular arrhythmias. Because caffeine has favorable dialyzable properties, including low molecular weight, low protein binding, and a relatively small volume of distribution, extracorporeal toxin removal may play a critical therapeutic role in severe intoxication refractory to conventional supportive and antiarrhythmic management. We report the case of a previously healthy 16-year-old Iranian adolescent girl who intentionally ingested 10.8 g of caffeine in a suicide attempt. Approximately two hours after ingestion, she presented with markedly reduced consciousness, agitation, generalized tremor, intermittent tonic/myoclonic seizure-like activity, sinus tachycardia (180-190 beats/min), hypokalemia (serum potassium 2.7 mEq/L), primary metabolic acidosis, significant rhabdomyolysis, and electrocardiographic abnormalities including mild QRS widening and QTc prolongation (~ 500 ms). Urine toxicology screening was positive for caffeine, supporting the diagnosis in conjunction with the clear ingestion history and subsequent patient confirmation. Despite early airway protection, gastrointestinal decontamination, electrolyte and acid-base correction, dual antiarrhythmic therapy with amiodarone and lidocaine, and repeated synchronized electrical cardioversion, she developed recurrent refractory sustained ventricular tachycardia, transient progression to asystole requiring cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and persistent severe metabolic instability. Emergency intermittent hemodialysis was initiated approximately 3-4 h after emergency department arrival, resulting in rapid correction of metabolic acidosis, complete cessation of malignant ventricular arrhythmias, and sustained restoration of stable sinus rhythm. The patient subsequently demonstrated progressive neurological recovery without persistent cardiac or neurological sequelae. This case highlights the potentially catastrophic cardiovascular consequences of massive caffeine intoxication and emphasizes the importance of early recognition, aggressive supportive care, rapid correction of metabolic abnormalities, and timely escalation to extracorporeal toxin removal in refractory cases. In patients with persistent malignant ventricular arrhythmias despite optimized pharmacologic and electrical management, intermittent hemodialysis may represent a life-saving therapeutic intervention capable of rapidly reversing toxicity and improving clinical outcomes.

title: Changes in speech reflect changes in psychotic symptom severity: a longitudinal natural language processing analysis.
abstract: The usefulness of automated speech and language markers to monitor or predict psychotic symptoms depends on their ability to detect changes in mental state. To date, research linking psychosis and Natural Language Processing (NLP) has been conducted almost exclusively using cross-sectional experimental designs, limiting insight into how intraindividual speech changes relate to symptoms and functioning. Therefore, here we examined the speech of 95 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia (n = 70) or schizoaffective disorder (n = 25) in a longitudinal design. Speech samples (using the Narrative of Emotions Task) and clinical ratings (PANSS, MINI-ICF) were collected at baseline and again at six-month follow-up. We computed longitudinal changes in eight NLP markers reflecting speech quantity, lexical and syntactic complexity, semantic similarity and connectivity. Our results replicated established associations between NLP metrics and clinical symptoms at baseline, for example local semantic similarity between adjacent sentences was negatively correlated with the PANSS negative symptom scale. Longitudinal analyses showed that measures of moving average type-token ratio, total token count, semantic similarity and graph connectivity were most sensitive to intraindividual changes in symptom severity and functional impairment. Finally, partial least squares regression yielded a significant association between longitudinal changes in these metrics and a component reflecting change in total and negative symptoms. Overall, our findings support the potential of NLP methods to help monitor symptoms for individuals with psychotic disorders. By enabling the early detection of symptom worsening, NLP tools could enable more timely intervention to prevent more serious illness.

title: From Synapses to Circuits: A Systematic Review of How Developmental Ethanol Exposure Alters Excitation-Inhibition Balance.
abstract: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a prevalent cause of neurodevelopmental impairment associated with lifelong cognitive and behavioral deficits. These difficulties may arise partly because developmental ethanol exposure disrupts the balance between excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) signaling. Acute ethanol exposure can suppress excitation through NMDA receptors and enhance inhibition through GABA_A receptors, thereby reducing neural activity. However, its longer-term effects on synaptic communication in the developing brain remain unclear. We systematically reviewed studies published from 2000 through December 2025 that used whole-cell electrophysiology to measure excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs and IPSCs) following developmental alcohol exposure. The review was limited to rat and mouse studies because these species are the principal experimental models of developmental ethanol exposure and allow comparisons across established developmental stages. Whole-cell studies were selected because they provide direct, cell-resolved measurements of spontaneous and miniature postsynaptic currents; field recordings, EEG, and other network-level approaches were outside the predefined scope. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. Sixteen examined inhibitory currents, 20 examined excitatory currents, and nine assessed E/I balance. Most studies reported increased frequencies of miniature or spontaneous IPSCs following developmental ethanol exposure. In contrast, EPSC frequency varied by brain region and developmental time point, with both increases and decreases reported. No consistent directional shift emerged among studies assessing E/I balance. Developmental ethanol exposure therefore appears to alter inhibitory synaptic transmission more consistently than excitatory transmission, while its overall effects on E/I balance are heterogeneous and circuit-dependent. These findings highlight the need for systematic, region-specific, and developmentally targeted studies to clarify how altered synaptic signaling contributes to cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in FASD.

title: Epigenetic modulation of the skeletal muscle methylome in a hind-limb unloading model.
abstract: Skeletal muscle exhibits remarkable plasticity, continually adapting to physiological and environmental stressors through coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic mechanisms. To our knowledge, this is the first study investigating the whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) of the gastrocnemius muscle of mice in a hind-limb unloading (HLU) model, to characterise genome-wide DNA methylation. HLU mice exhibited reduced gastrocnemius weight, consistent with muscle atrophy, impaired grip strength, and shorter wire hanging times. Histological analysis revealed smaller fiber sizes and fewer myonuclei per fiber, accompanied by a significant reduction in myonuclear domain (MND) size, suggesting compromised transcriptional support per nucleus. These structural and functional changes were accompanied by differential methylation of genes associated with anabolic and cytoskeletal pathways. Following quality control (coverage ≥ 10×; q < 0.01; methylation difference ≥ 25%), 6,892 differentially methylated regions (DMRs) were identified and annotated to genomic and functional features. HLU induced widespread CpG methylation remodelling, with 4,755 regions (69.0%) hypermethylated and 2,137 (31.0%) hypomethylated, indicating a genome-wide shift toward hypermethylation. Pathway enrichment analyses were performed to identify the biological relevance of methylation changes. Most DMRs were localised within promoter and gene-body regions, particularly across chromosomes 1, 7, and 11, which contain regulators of muscle metabolism, cytoskeletal organisation, and energy homeostasis. Hypermethylation of genes such as Atp6v1h, Sox17, and Rgs20 was associated with pathways involved in lysosomal function, angiogenesis, and G-protein signalling, potentially reflecting metabolic downscaling and reduced contractile demand. Conversely, hypomethylation of structural and cytoskeletal genes may support maintenance of mechanical stability and stress resilience. Enrichment of calcium signalling, MAPK, Rap1, Wnt, oxidative phosphorylation, and autophagy pathways underscores coordinated epigenetic regulation of contraction-metabolism and mitochondrial adaptation. Together, our findings suggest that HLU is associated with coordinated epigenetic and phenotypic remodelling in skeletal muscle, with CpG methylation representing a potential regulatory layer involved in adaptation to mechanical unloading.

title: Expression of nuclear factor kappa B-associated long non-coding RNAs in drug-naïve and valproic acid-treated epilepsy patients.
abstract: Epilepsy has a complex etiopathogenesis and frequently shows resistance to conventional antiseizure medications, underscoring the need for a deeper mechanistic understanding of the disease. Accumulating evidence implicates NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammation in epileptogenesis, and several long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are known to regulate this pathway. However, the expression patterns of the NF-κB-associated lncRNAs UCA1, ANRIL, and NKILA in epilepsy, and whether antiseizure medications can modulate them, remain largely unknown. This study therefore assessed these lncRNAs, together with the inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6, in drug-naïve and valproic acid (VPA)-treated epileptic patients compared with healthy controls. In a prospective, multicenter study with 120 adults, participants were divided into three groups: drug-naïve patients, VPA-treated patients, and healthy volunteers. Early morning blood samples were collected to measure serum levels of the selected lncRNAs and cytokines. Correlations between molecular markers and seizure parameters were examined. Serum IL-1β, IL-6, UCA1, and ANRIL were significantly higher in drug-naïve patients than in healthy controls (p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p = 0.003, and p = 0.014, respectively), whereas NKILA showed no significant difference (p = 0.484). Compared with drug-naïve patients, VPA-treated patients showed no significant difference in IL-1β (p = 0.056) or IL-6 (p = 1.00); in the age- and sex-adjusted Bayesian model, UCA1 was significantly lower in the VPA group compared to the drug-naive group (p = 0.015) and no longer differed from controls (p = 0.424), whereas ANRIL remained largely unchanged. Serum IL-1β had a significant positive correlation with IL-6 (ρ = 0.58, p < 0.001) and ANRIL (ρ = 0.20, p = 0.028), and in drug-naïve patients seizure severity significantly correlate positively with UCA1 (ρ = 0.41, p = 0.009). On ROC analysis, IL-1β and IL-6 best discriminated untreated patients from controls (AUC = 0.84 and 0.96, respectively). These findings indicate heightened systemic inflammation in untreated epilepsy and support IL-1β and IL-6 as potential candidate biomarkers, with UCA1 as a potentially treatment-responsive lncRNA. Our results identify serum UCA1 as the most notably altered lncRNA, significantly elevated in untreated epilepsy and potentially responsive to valproic acid. While IL-1β and IL-6 reflected the accompanying inflammation. These findings warrant further validation as candidate biomarker.

title: Birth position and tissue context influence Bipolar Cell translocation mode in the developing retina.
abstract: Neuronal translocation is essential for establishing functional tissue architecture in the developing central nervous system. While many of the cell-intrinsic mechanisms driving translocation have been identified, how these strategies adapt to dynamic developmental tissue changes remains less understood. Here, we address this question using retinal Bipolar Cells as a model as they are generated across unlaminated and laminated stages. This enables direct comparison of neuronal translocation modes and dynamics across development. We show that the mode of movement of Bipolar Cells changes depending on tissue lamination state. Bipolar Cells born before photoreceptor layer formation undergo directed, microtubule-dependent somal translocation as seen for other early born neurons. In contrast, later-born Bipolar Cells exhibit more passive and less directed displacement that seems to be mostly driven by collective tissue movements. Interference with tissue-wide movements reduces this displacement, while disrupting photoreceptor layer formation leads to directed translocation also at later developmental stages. Independent of strategy, cells achieve accurate laminar positioning. Together, this shows that tissue context can influence cell movement modes, a principle likely relevant across developing neural and other tissues.

title: Letter to the editor. The making of a neurosurgeon: Stoic askēsis and the cultivation of surgical virtue: Comment on "Non-technical skills for neurosurgeons: An international survey".
Calpeptin attenuates LPS-induced ventriculomegaly in neonatal mice.
abstract: Acute inflammatory insults in the developing brain can produce ventriculomegaly, but underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We tested whether preventive calpeptin treatment modified the phenotype induced by intraventricular lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in neonatal mice. Ventricular-volume analysis included vehicle (12 pups/4 litters), LPS (8 pups/3 litters), and LPS + calpeptin (10 pups/2 litters). Calpeptin reduced mean ventricular volume by 72% relative to LPS (2.48 versus 8.92 mm3); the difference persisted in a mixed-effects model with litter as a random intercept (-0.61 log10 mm3, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.20, p = 0.004). Survival analysis included vehicle (13 pups/4 litters), LPS (26 pups/5 litters), and LPS + calpeptin (12 pups/2 litters). Observed endpoint survival was 10/12 with calpeptin versus 10/26 with LPS, but the litter-level comparison was not significant, and pronounced between-litter heterogeneity and only two calpeptin litters preclude a definitive treatment-effect inference; survival remains exploratory. Cortical DiI vascular labeling and VE-cadherin immunofluorescence were obtained from one litter per group and are descriptive, not measures of blood-brain barrier permeability. In cultured primary brain microvascular endothelial cells, LPS increased permeability and the approximately 95/130 kDa VE-cadherin-immunoreactive band ratio. Calpeptin and TLR4 inhibition reduced the band-ratio increase but did not significantly attenuate permeability relative to LPS. Calpeptin is not protease- or isoform-selective, and target engagement was not measured. Thus, the findings suggest a contribution from calpeptin-sensitive protease activity without identifying the responsible protease, confirming cleavage of the lower band, or demonstrating endothelial barrier protection in vivo.

title: Interventions to prevent suicide and suicidal thoughts or behaviours in the perinatal period: a global mixed-methods systematic review.
abstract: Suicide is a leading cause of maternal death during the perinatal period. While routine enquiry and identification is widely recommended, evidence on comprehensive interventions remains limited. This review evaluated global evidence on the effectiveness of interventions for perinatal suicide, associated thoughts and behaviours, and key implementation features. We conducted a mixed-methods systematic review using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology. We searched eight databases and other sources from inception to December 3, 2025, for global evidence across all income settings without language restrictions. We included studies evaluating interventions, programmes or strategies reporting on our primary outcome: perinatal suicide or suicidal thoughts or behaviours (including ideation, self-harm, attempts) during pregnancy or one year after birth. Data were extracted and appraised for methodological quality. Meta-analysis was not possible due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity; data were synthesised using a convergent integrated approach. PROSPERO: CRD42025625903. We screened 27,045 records; 19 records representing nine studies were included: three randomised controlled trials, one secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial, one non-randomised controlled trial, one quasi-experimental study, one cross-sectional descriptive study, one economic modelling, and one qualitative study. Studies were conducted between 2011 and 2025 in North America, Europe and Asia and included 3613 participants from at risk or disadvantaged populations across eight studies, plus a simulated cohort of 1000. We found trials of indirect clinical interventions targeting parenting or attachment did not reduce suicidality, whereas task-shared behavioural activation psychotherapy targeting depressive drivers, was associated with an 80% reduction in odds of suicidal ideation at three months in a secondary trial analysis. System or community-level strategies in three trials and the modelling were associated with reduced suicide or suicidal ideation by integrating routine screening within multidisciplinary pathways that ensured immediate linkage to care. Informal or crisis support mechanisms facilitated immediate access and worked as protective buffers against self-harm in two feasibility and qualitative studies; faith practices helped counter barriers to formal care while helplines remained limited by them. Our results suggest that suicide prevention could be improved by embedding routine identification within coordinated health and community safety nets ensuring immediate linkage to care. Expanding evidence-based psychological care and task-sharing targeting depressive drivers of suicidality may help at-risk women receive timely support. Future research explicitly designed and powered for perinatal suicide prevention is needed. The National Institute for Health and Care Research.

title: Implementation of scientific evidence into rheumatological care-the viewpoint of the EULAR.
authors: van der Helm van Mil Annette Helena Maria
abstract: The gap between scientific discoveries and bedside application remains one of the most significant challenges in modern healthcare. Implementation science can aid this process by ensuring that health practices evolve alongside scientific progress rather than lagging years behind. This viewpoint focuses on the efforts of the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology to foster the implementation process of recommendations for rheumatic and musculoskeletal disease by addressing implementation strategies and by outlining barriers and facilitators for supporting interdisciplinary and patient-centred care.

title: Internet-delivered acceptance-based CBT for frequent migraine in routine care as add-on to medical treatment 12-month results: A randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Frequent episodic and chronic migraine are associated with disability, psychological distress, and reduced quality of life. This study evaluated the long-term effects of I AM, an individually tailored, therapist-guided, acceptance-based, Internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy (ICBT) programme combined with treatment as usual (TAU) in Swedish primary care. The aim was to evaluate the effects of acceptance-based Internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy + TAU compared with TAU alone on migraine frequency, pain intensity, migraine-related disability, and mental health and well-being. In this randomized controlled study, 154 participants with frequent episodic or chronic migraine were randomized to I AM + TAU or TAU alone. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, post-treatment, and at 6- and 12-month follow-ups. Intervention effects were evaluated using time × condition interactions, with baseline as the reference timepoint. For migraine-related disability (HIT-6), the time × condition interaction was significant at 12 months (β = -3.406, 95% CI [-5.970, -0.841], p = .010), indicating a greater reduction from baseline in the I AM + TAU group compared with TAU alone. For mental health and well-being (MHC-SF), significant time × condition interactions were observed at post-treatment (β = 5.472, 95% CI [0.071, 10.873], p = .047) and 12 months (β = 5.563, 95% CI [0.176, 10.950], p = .043), indicating greater improvements in the I AM + TAU group. The interaction at 6 months was not significant for either HIT-6 or MHC-SF. No significant time × condition interactions were observed for number of monthly migraine days or pain intensity at post-treatment, 6 months, or 12 months. I AM combined with TAU resulted in greater reduction in migraine-related disability at 12 months and in mental health and well-being at post-treatment and 12 months compared with TAU alone. No differences between the groups were observed on number of monthly migraine days or pain intensity. These findings suggest that acceptance-based ICBT may provide benefits primarily in reducing the functional burden of migraine and supporting psychological well-being rather than in reducing migraine frequency or pain intensity.

title: Allele-selective and pan-allelic huntingtin lowering differentially affect neuronal homeostasis and BDNF transport.
abstract: Huntington's disease (HD) is a devastating genetic neurodegenerative disorder caused by the abnormal expansion of CAG-repeats, which encode a poly-glutamine stretch in the huntingtin (HTT) protein. HD patients typically carry one wild-type and one mutant allele. We compared pan-allelic (PAN) and allele-selective antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) targeting a single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the sequence encoding the mutant isoform in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons carrying 69Q or 109Q alleles. SNP ASO selectively reduced mut-HTT mRNA and protein, while PAN ASO lowered both alleles. Proteomic profiling revealed that allele-selective mutant HTT lowering preserved pathways for neuronal morphogenesis, synaptic function, and mitochondrial metabolism. In human HD neuronal networks reconstituted in microfluidic devices, SNP ASO maintained synaptic connectivity, network synchronization, and BDNF vesicle trafficking. By contrast, PAN ASO impaired axonal transport, energy metabolism, activity-dependent survival signaling, and network oscillations. These findings support the rationale for allele-selective HTT silencing to preserve neuronal functions during HTT lowering while limiting extensive depletion of total HTT.

title: Cellular senescence in diabetic retinopathy: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic targeting.
journal: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the leading cause of vision loss in the working-age population, traditionally attributed to metabolic disorders and microvascular damage induced by chronic hyperglycemia. Emerging evidence indicates that cellular senescence acts as a critical upstream driver of DR, with senescent cells accumulating in the retina and secreting a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors that promote chronic inflammation, pathological angiogenesis, and disruption of the blood-retinal barrier (BRB). This review adopts a neurovascular unit (NVU) perspective to synthesize cell-type-specific senescence phenotypes in the diabetic retina, emphasizing that endothelial cell, pericyte, retinal pigment epithelium, microglial, and retinal ganglion cell senescence constitute an interconnected pathological network rather than isolated events. NVU-wide senescence establishes a self-reinforcing cycle: senescent endothelial and pericyte dysfunction drives vascular instability; retinal pigment epithelial cells senescence compromises the outer BRB; and glial cell and retinal ganglion cell senescence amplifies neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. We dissect key molecular drivers-oxidative DNA damage, epigenetic reprogramming (miRNA/Sirtuins), mitophagy impairment, and SASP-mediated inflammatory feedforward-and critically evaluate emerging senotherapeutics (senolytics, senomorphics, and precision delivery platforms) within an evidence-graded framework. Cellular senescence establishes a progressive senescence-inflammation vicious cycle in DR, affecting multiple interconnected cell types within the NVU and causing neurovascular dysfunction. Targeting cellular senescence through senescent cell clearance, SASP inhibition, mitochondrial homeostasis regulation, and epigenetic modulation offers promising new therapeutic directions. With the advancement of novel senotherapeutics and precision technologies, personalized early treatment and retinal repair for DR may become achievable in the future.

title: Is liquid biopsy in oncology cost-effective? A comparative analysis and systematic review.
abstract: To describe cost-effectiveness trends in oncological liquid biopsy (LB) through harmonized comparative analyses across countries, cancer types, technologies, and clinical applications. Economic evaluations reporting incremental costs and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) for oncological LB-related strategies and comparators. MEDLINE (via PubMed) and Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using CHEQUE, with mean methodological and reporting scores of 79.7% and 85.5%, respectively. Economic inputs were harmonized to EUR 2024. Incremental net monetary benefit (INMB) was recalculated under eight willingness-to-pay (WTP) criteria, using median INMB as the primary descriptive outcome. Complementary analyses examined the so-called ΔWTP% (i.e., the percentage ratio between the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) and the WTP threshold), means, subgroups, scenario eligibility, and sensitivity to WTP selection. Twenty-one studies contributed 43 modeled scenarios. Median INMB was positive under all eight WTP criteria (+€79.52 to +€5091.21 per patient); eight scenarios were dominant. Seventeen scenarios (39.53%) changed economic classification across thresholds. INMB and ΔWTP% agreed in all 328 eligible scenario-threshold comparisons. Under the common Italian GDP×2 WTP, 79.07% of scenarios and 96.97% of subgroups had favorable INMB, with an overall median of +€1560.07 per patient. Two cost-saving scenarios with negative QALYs highlighted ethical and distributional trade-offs. Differences in clinical pathways, model assumptions, and local costs, together with non-independent scenarios and unavailable patient-level data, limit setting-specific interpretation. LB showed broadly favorable but context-dependent economic potential. Median INMB and complementary sensitivity analyses support transparent comparisons; clinical implementation requires locally calibrated evaluation. No external funding. PROSPERO ID = CRD420250652247; absent pre-published review protocol.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Nanoparticle-Mediated Targeted Drug Delivery in Neurodegenerative Diseases.
abstract: With global population aging, the incidence of neurodegenerative diseases continues to rise, and the blood-brain barrier (BBB) excludes approximately 98% of small-molecule drugs and nearly all large-molecule biologics from the central nervous system (CNS), so conventional small-molecule pharmacotherapy is largely limited to symptom modulation. Nanodrug delivery systems, including ligand-engineered polymeric, lipid, and inorganic nanoparticles as well as naturally secreted extracellular vesicles, have been proposed as a way to overcome the BBB and modulate disease pathways, and most of the supporting evidence currently derives from rodent models. This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms by which these systems cross or bypass the BBB, summarizes representative disease-specific interventions in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and multiple sclerosis, and critically discusses translational bottlenecks, with the explicit aim of distinguishing established mechanisms from preclinical observations and clarifying the path to clinical investigation. We deliberately limited in scope to systems for which mechanistic and delivery data are available, and the rapid pace of the field means that conclusions about clinical efficacy cannot be drawn from the present preclinical literature. Nevertheless, it still provides valuable insights for research in this field.

title: Linagliptin as a Multi-Target Neuroprotective Agent in Cognitive Disorders: Molecular Mechanisms and Translational Challenges-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Cognitive disorders, which are characterized by progressive impairment of memory, language, and other cognitive functions, are a growing global health challenge. Currently, there are limited therapeutic options available to prevent or reverse the progression of these disorders. Linagliptin, an approved treatment for type 2 diabetes, has recently emerged as a neuroprotective agent, offering benefits beyond its glucose-lowering effects. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that linagliptin improves cognitive performance and protects neuronal integrity in various experimental models, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), cerebral ischemia, diabetic cognitive dysfunction, demyelination, and toxicant-induced cognitive impairment. The neuroprotective actions of linagliptin are mediated through multiple mechanisms, including the attenuation of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress, as well as the inhibition of apoptotic pathways, preservation of blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity, and enhancement of neurovascular function. This multi-target profile highlights the potential of linagliptin as a promising therapeutic candidate for cognitive disorders. Despite encouraging preclinical findings, the CARMELINA and CAROLINA-COGNITION trials found no significant cognitive benefit of linagliptin, highlighting the gap between preclinical evidence and demonstrated clinical efficacy. This narrative review summarizes the molecular mechanisms and preclinical and clinical evidence regarding the effects of linagliptin in cognitive disorders, with particular emphasis on its potential neuroprotective mechanisms and translational challenges.

title: EGTool: an evolutionary genome topology tool for multiscale comparative genomics.
abstract: Increased phylogenomic sampling and availability of thousands of high-quality genome assemblies require tools to simultaneously analyze changes to both chromosomal and subchromosomal genome architecture. Recently, we proposed an evolutionary genome topology (EGT) approach to identify and associate genome structural changes with evolutionary transitions. In this Application Note, we provide a generalized implementation of this approach, which we call EGTool. EGTool compares genomes to each other (multigenome topology) or loci to each other across genomes (multilocus topology), accepts arbitrary positional and orthology inputs, works in base-pair or index coordinates, projects new genomes onto an existing embedding without refitting, and recovers the features that characterize any chosen region of the projection via inverse transform. A 510-genome, 1274-locus example is included to illustrate these functionalities and can be run on a laptop within 30 min. EGTool is implemented in Python (≥3.8) with dependencies on NumPy, pandas, umap-learn, matplotlib, NetworkX, and scikit-learn. It is installable via pip after cloning the repository. The optional ancestral linkage group detection step (egtool alg) requires R. A Perl script is provided for converting genome annotation files to the input .chrom format. Source code, example data, and tutorials are available at: https://bitbucket.org/viemet/egtool/src/main/.

title: Neuroimaging of Anxiety in Mild Cognitive Impairment: Integrating Structural, Functional, Molecular, and Network Perspectives-A Narrative Review.
abstract: This narrative review summarizes neuroimaging evidence on the neurobiological correlates of anxiety symptoms in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) across the Alzheimer's disease continuum. A literature search was conducted in PubMed from 1 January 2015 to 30 June 2026. Structural magnetic resonance imaging studies link anxiety to atrophy in medial temporal and prefrontal-limbic regions, with white matter disruption in the cingulum bundle and uncinate fasciculus. Functional magnetic resonance imaging shows altered interactions among the default mode network, salience network, and central executive network. Molecular imaging points to limbic glucose hypometabolism, amyloid deposition, and neuroinflammation. Emerging vascular and peripheral biomarker data further implicate blood-brain barrier disruption and gut-brain axis alterations. Most of the literature is cross-sectional and relies on heterogeneous anxiety assessments. Findings are further complicated by symptom overlap with depression and other neuropsychiatric manifestations, and anxiety-specific imaging studies in MCI are relatively scarce. Direct evidence specific to anxiety in MCI remains limited; some findings discussed here are derived from studies of Alzheimer's disease dementia or general neuropsychiatric symptoms and should be interpreted accordingly. Longitudinal multimodal designs, standardized anxiety-specific instruments, and integrative models linking symptom dimensions to imaging and fluid biomarkers are needed to disentangle whether anxiety in MCI represents an early marker of neurodegeneration, a disease-course modifier, or both.

title: Maniform Presentation of Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia Mimicking Late-Onset Mania: A Diagnostic Challenge.
abstract: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that may initially present with behavioral and affective symptoms, often mimicking primary psychiatric conditions, such as bipolar disorder, leading to frequent misdiagnosis. We report the case of a 70-year-old woman with no prior psychiatric history who presented with a first episode of maniform behavior, characterized by euphoria, disinhibition, decreased need for sleep, impulsive spending, and socially inappropriate conduct, mimicking late-onset bipolar disorder. Neuropsychological evaluation revealed significant executive dysfunction. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated bilateral frontal and anterior temporal lobe atrophy consistent with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD). This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing late-onset manic syndromes from neurodegenerative disease. It underscores the importance of integrating clinical history, cognitive assessment, and neuroimaging to improve diagnostic accuracy and avoid misdiagnosis.

title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Nuances in Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy-Related Inflammation: Case Reports and Literature Review.
abstract: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy-related inflammation (CAA-ri) is a rare autoimmune response to vascular β-amyloid deposition that poses a significant diagnostic challenge. Its clinicoradiological criteria require evidence of cortical or subcortical microhemorrhage or superficial siderosis markers whose detection depends on the field strength and sequence of the study. We describe two cases that bracket this problem. In the first case, a 74-year-old woman presented with subacute lethargy and a right parietal lesion initially concerning for an infiltrating low-grade glioma on 1.5 T MRI. Two gradient-echo studies at 1.5 T 1 month apart showed no microhemorrhages, and she, therefore, did not satisfy the criteria for probably CAA-ri. Subsequent ultra-high-field 7 T MRI demonstrated numerous cortical microhemorrhages not captured on conventional imaging, shifting the clinical suspicion toward CAA-ri. Brain biopsy was performed confirming vascular amyloid involvement. The patient experienced spontaneous radiographic resolution without corticosteroid therapy. In the second case, an 84-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and dementia presented with progressive confusion. Neuroimaging revealed severe, confluent white matter hyperintensities and multiple microhemorrhages consistent with CAA-ri, satisfying criteria for probably CAA-ri on 1.5 T imaging alone. Unlike the first case, this patient received high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, resulting in rapid clinical stabilization and subsequent resolution of vasogenic edema on follow-up imaging. Together, these cases demonstrate divergent diagnostic outcomes under identical criteria. One patient was identified within days on conventional imaging while the other underwent extensive neoplastic evaluation. The determinant was the detectability of the microhemorrhages on the acquired sequence rather than difference in disease phenotype. This limitation extends to screening for antiamyloid monoclonal antibody therapy in which eligibility is determined by microhemorrhage counts obtained on conventional MRI. Maintaining a high index of suspicion for CAA-ri is essential when evaluating atypical intracranial lesions in older adults to ensure timely diagnosis and appropriate therapeutic management.

title: The Copper-Zinc Balance in Hypertension: A Cross-Sectional Study From Bangladesh.
abstract: Hypertension (HTN) is a major public health problem, and disturbances in trace-element homeostasis may contribute to its pathogenesis. Copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn) are involved in antioxidant defense and vascular function, while their relative balance may be reflected by the copper-to-zinc (Cu/Zn) ratio. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association of serum Cu, Zn, and Cu/Zn ratio with HTN among adults attending Bangladesh Medical University (BMU), Dhaka. This cross-sectional comparative study was conducted in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, BMU, among 100 adults aged ≥40 years, comprising 46 hypertensive and 54 normotensive participants recruited from the Cardiology and Medicine outpatient departments. Serum Cu and Zn levels were measured using standard spectrophotometric methods, and the Cu/Zn ratio was calculated. Lifestyle factors, excess salt intake, dyslipidemia, and body mass index were also assessed. Independent-samples t-test, Chi-square test, and Spearman's correlation analysis were used as appropriate. Binary logistic regression was performed to determine the independent association of serum Zn and Cu/Zn ratio with HTN after adjustment for dyslipidemia and excess salt intake. A p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. The median age was 50 years in both groups. Excess salt intake was significantly more common among hypertensive participants (27; 58.70%) than normotensive participants (19; 35.19%), p=0.019, as was dyslipidemia (23; 50.00% vs. 10; 18.52%, p=0.003). Serum Cu levels did not differ significantly between hypertensive and normotensive participants (101.42±29.12 vs. 94.14±24.92 µg/dL, p=0.187). In contrast, serum Zn levels were significantly lower in the hypertensive group (63.46±19.01 vs. 73.75±24.54 µg/dL, p=0.015), while the Cu/Zn ratio was significantly higher (1.53±0.61 vs. 1.22±0.49, p=0.007). Serum Zn showed significant negative correlations with systolic blood pressure (SBP) (ρ = -0.412, p<0.001) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP) (ρ = -0.210, p=0.036), whereas the Cu/Zn ratio showed significant positive correlations with SBP (ρ=0.412, p<0.001) and DBP (ρ=0.278, p=0.005). Serum Cu showed no significant correlation with either SBP or DBP. After adjustment for dyslipidemia and excess salt intake, the fourth quartile of the Cu/Zn ratio was independently associated with HTN, with approximately 3.7-fold higher odds than the first quartile (adjusted odds ratio=3.723, p=0.043), whereas serum Zn showed no independent association. Serum Cu was not significantly associated with HTN, whereas lower serum Zn and a higher Cu/Zn ratio were observed among hypertensive individuals. The Cu/Zn ratio showed significant correlations with both SBP and DBP and remained independently associated with HTN after adjustment for selected confounders. The Cu/Zn ratio may therefore have potential as an additional marker of trace-element imbalance in HTN; however, larger prospective studies are required to establish its clinical and causal significance.

title: A mutation in the conserved NPxY motif of β integrin PAT-3 alters outgrowth of neuronal dendritic spines.
abstract: Integrins are heterodimeric transmembrane receptors that are critical in many biological processes, including neuronal development. Here we investigate integrin signaling in the outgrowth of dendritic spines on C. elegans GABAergic neurons using mutations engineered within the membrane-distal NPxY motif of the β integrin subunit PAT-3 . We found a Y/E substitution, but not Y/A or Y/F substitutions, reduced dendritic spine number and misoriented spines. The Y/E substitution in the NPxY motif also altered the distribution of the presynaptic scaffold CLA-1 , suggesting roles in both pre- and postsynaptic development. Our findings implicate integrin activation through the NPxY motif in synapse formation/maturation.

title: Generation of depolarization-responsive dental stem cell-derived neural-like spheroids using a micropatterned chip platform.
abstract: Dental stem cells represent an accessible adult stem cell source with neuronal affinity due to their cranial neural crest origin, yet dental-derived neural-like spheroid models often suffer from heterogeneous differentiation, limited organization, and poor reproducibility. Here, we established a stepwise workflow to induce neurogenic differentiation of dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and organize them into spatially controlled, depolarization-responsive neural-like spheroids using a micropatterned culture platform. Seven-day neurogenic induction generated Neuro-DPSCs with marked morphological remodeling, neurite-like processes, and increased expression of neural lineage markers including TUJ1, NSE, MAP2, NeuN, and NEFM. In 3D culture, Neuro-DPSCs self-assembled into spheroidal aggregates, while substrate wettability strongly influenced aggregation and outgrowth. Hydrophobic surfaces promoted spheroid formation but limited long-term maintenance due to free-floating aggregation. To improve spatial control, a micropatterned platform was applied to define adhesive contact points, constrain spheroid positioning, and guide inter-spheroid neurite-like network formation. The resulting spheroids showed enrichment of gene networks associated with neurite-like organization, axon guidance, synaptic vesicle biology, neurotransmitter-related pathways, and receptor signaling, together with KCl-induced depolarization-responsive calcium activity. These findings demonstrate that neurogenic priming combined with micropattern-guided assembly provides a controllable workflow for generating spatially organized neural-like DPSC spheroids.

title: Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Narrative Review of Blood-Based Biomarkers and Detection Methods.
abstract: Given the prevalence of mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) and sports-related concussion, the development of efficient diagnosis methods is essential. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography are standard imaging modalities in traumatic brain injury assessment, they frequently fail to detect the subtle structural and metabolic changes associated with mTBI. Furthermore, while cognitive tests like the Immediate Post-Concussion Assessment and Cognitive Testing and the Sports Concussion Assessment Tool 5 have been developed, fluid-based biomarkers provide a cheaper and quicker method to identify mTBI. Using the PubMed database, we searched for English-language articles on mTBI biomarkers. Conventional biomarkers (e.g., glial fibrillary acidic protein, neuron-specific enolase, tau) frequently show statistically significant group-level differences after mTBI, but their individual-level diagnostic performance is often moderate, with overlapping distributions. As a result, single markers alone may not reliably distinguish mTBI from controls or from other neurological conditions. Biomarkers can detect differences between mTBI and control patients, but the literature suggests that detectors such as neurogranin are not significant indicators of mTBI. Moreover, studies showed that alpha-synuclein increases during the acute phase of mTBI, yet it has been found that lower α-synuclein levels are associated with mTBI in trauma patients. Due to these discrepancies, multi-biomarker panels may be the most comprehensive way to detect mTBI in the acute phase. While some developments are promising, the limitations associated with the current biomarkers warrant comprehensive studies to assess their effectiveness. In clinical practice, these proteins are measured using automated electrochemiluminescence immunoassays that are inexpensive, allow single-sample testing, and yield results in ∼20 min. Access is the constraint, as these analyzers are hospital-based; therefore, point-of-care (e.g., finger-prick) tests remain a priority. Conventional enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay are research tools and are less suitable for acute-care workflows. Attention should be directed toward the development of technologies to measure mTBI biomarkers pitch-side so that head injuries can be diagnosed immediately after injury.

title: Slow-Wave Enhancement Reduces Axonal Injury in Murine Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of death and disability as well as impaired cognition and sleep-wake abnormalities. The pathological hallmark of TBI is disturbed axonal transport and accumulation of proteins, leading to diffuse axonal injury (DAI). Recent studies suggest a role for slow-wave sleep (SWS) in the clearance of harmful extracellular proteins and functional recovery. Our group previously found that increasing SWS after TBI in rats improved cognition and decreased accumulation of injury-related histological markers in cortex and hippocampus, indicating a neuroprotective role of SWS. Though growing evidence suggests that sleep can improve the outcome of TBI, prior mouse models of TBI were incompatible with sleep recordings. In the current study, we modified the classical weight-drop mouse model to be compatible with a headset for recording electroencephalogram (EEG) and electromyogram, and to replicate effects of SWS modulation on TBI outcome measures. The resulting mild TBI mouse model shows cognitive impairment, EEG abnormalities, and DAI. Such DAI was reduced following treatment with sodium oxybate during the first 3 days after trauma, concomitant with increased slow-wave activity. Chemogenetic modulation of basal forebrain cholinergic neurons, on the other hand, did not reduce slow-wave activity. Overall, in the present study, we characterized an adapted weight-drop mouse TBI model for studying the relationship between sleep and TBI and provided additional evidence on involvement of sleep in neuronal recovery.

title: The pharmacotherapeutic use of clozapine in older adults: A narrative review.
abstract: Clozapine remains the gold-standard treatment for refractory schizophrenia, yet its use in older adults is often limited by concerns regarding tolerability, age-related pharmacokinetic changes, and the burden of medical comorbidities. This narrative review synthesises current evidence on clozapine use in older populations, with a focus on pharmacokinetic alterations, dosing strategies, comorbidity-related considerations, and clozapine's therapeutic benefits, safety, and risks. A primary aim is to review the nature of age-related pharmacokinetic changes and their cumulative impact over time. Aging is associated with changes in drug absorption, increased volume of distribution due to altered body composition, reduced hepatic blood flow, decreased cytochrome P450 enzyme activity, and impaired clearance, all of which may elevate clozapine and norclozapine plasma concentrations and increase susceptibility to adverse effects. Older adults are particularly vulnerable to sedation, orthostatic hypotension, anticholinergic effects, gastrointestinal hypomotility, falls, and serious adverse events including agranulocytosis and pneumonia. Polypharmacy and comorbidities such as hepatic conditions, obesity and cognitive impairment further complicate treatment and elevate the risk of drug interactions. Evidence supports a conservative "start low, go slow" approach, guided by therapeutic drug monitoring to determine clozapine concentrations, with many older adults achieving therapeutic benefit at lower doses than younger patients, alongside careful monitoring and individualized risk-benefit assessment. Understanding these age-related pharmacokinetic and clinical considerations is essential to optimise dosing, minimise toxicity, and enhance therapeutic outcomes in older patients. Further research is required to strengthen the evidence base and develop clear clinical guidelines for this growing population.

title: Impact of treatment mechanism on octave MSDA pathway scores in patients receiving ocrelizumab or natalizumab.
journal: Multiple sclerosis journal - experimental, translational and clinical
abstract: To compare MSDA Score and pathway scores between patients treated with ocrelizumab and natalizumab in real-world MS population. We conducted a cross-sectional observational study of patients treated with ocrelizumab or natalizumab at a tertiary MS center between June 2023 and February 2025. Octave MSDA results were linked to clinical and MRI data from electronic health records. Group differences in MSDA composite and pathway scores were evaluated using ordinal regression models adjusted for demographic and disease-related covariates. A total of 152 patients were included (105 ocrelizumab, and 47 natalizumab). Except for two natalizumab-treated patients (≥ 4 months), all patients had been on their current DMT for at least 6 months. Patients treated with ocrelizumab were significantly more likely to have low MSDA scores (MSDA ≤ 4) compared to those treated with natalizumab (98.1% vs. 66%), despite similar clinical and MRI outcomes. Patients on ocrelizumab also had lower scores in three biological pathways, including neuroinflammation (p < 0.001), immunomodulation (p < 0.001), and myelin biology (p = 0.002). Ocrelizumab-treated patients showed significantly lower Octave MSDA composite scores compared with natalizumab, independent of clinical and MRI findings, highlighting the importance of considering DMT mechanisms when interpreting serum biomarker profiles.

title: Alleviation of Symptom Burden Following Deep Brain Stimulation in Moderate to Severe Brain Injury.
abstract: Many patients experience high symptom burden for many years following moderate to severe traumatic brain injury (TBI). Here, we use the Rivermead Post-Concussion Symptoms Questionnaire (RPQ), a self-report questionnaire that tracks the severity of chronic symptoms that impact quality of life, to evaluate longitudinal changes following deep brain stimulation (DBS) in participants with chronic, moderate to severe TBI (msTBI) and to compare findings to the natural recovery observed in the TRACK-TBI Longitudinal cohort. The DBS cohort consisted of the five participants with msTBI in the CENTURY-S trial (CENtral Thalamic Deep Brain Stimulation for the Treatment of Traumatic Brain InjURY, NCT02881151) who received DBS. The total mean RPQ score decreased from 35.0 (SD 8.7) to 18.4 (SD 18.5). 3 participants reporting 10, 8, and 4 symptoms (of a possible 16) as moderate or severe at baseline reported 0 symptoms at this level at treatment end. A fourth participant showed a 50% decrease in the number of moderate to severe symptoms, from 10 to 5. A sample of 107 patients with msTBI from the TRACK-TBI Longitudinal study served as a comparison group. The TRACK-TBI Longitudinal RPQ total score remained stable from 1-year post-injury (mean 13.84. SD 12.61) to the first follow-up at either 2, 3, 4, or ≥5 years post-injury (mean 14.47. SD 12.98). More TRACK-TBI Longitudinal participants experienced worsening moderate to severe symptoms than improvement (increased: N = 44; decreased: N = 28; no change: N = 35). Participants in the CENTURY-S trial with chronic msTBI (3-18 years post injury) achieved marked improvements after DBS in total symptom burden and in the number of symptoms reported as moderate to severe in contrast to participants in the TRACK-Longitudinal sample whose RPQ scores remained stable. These observations suggest that DBS of the central lateral thalamus alleviates chronic TBI-related symptoms, surpassing the natural recovery documented in the TRACK-TBI Longitudinal cohort.

title: The Forgotten Search for an LSD "Antidote".
abstract: This commentary reconstructs a neglected early clinical finding in psychopharmacology: The mid-1950s clinical observation that chlorpromazine partially antagonizes the subjective effects of Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). Here, we provide the first English translation of the foundational 1955 study by Giberti and Gregoretti. This early work, alongside some contemporaneous and ethically abusive human experimentation funded by the Central Intelligence Agency of the federal government of the United States (CIA) under its MKULTRA program, demonstrated significant pharmacological blockade. However, this line of inquiry was severed from the scientific literature following the suppression of psychedelic research in the 1970s. Consequently, this clear drug-drug interaction remained an isolated clinical fact without a mechanistic explanation for decades. Modern neuropharmacology has now elucidated the precise receptor-level basis: Chlorpromazine acts as an antagonist at the 5-HT2A receptor, the primary molecular target of classic psychedelics like LSD. Thus, contemporary receptor knowledge validates and explains these prescient, premechanistic clinical insights.

title: Does the sheath fit? Microgliosis-mediated myelin remodeling drives interneuronopathy.
GLP-1(9-37) Improves Left Ventricular Function in a Murine Model of Cardiac Pressure Overload by Promoting Mitochondrial Biogenesis.
authors: van der Vorst Emiel P C
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin hormone that is released in response to nutrient intake and inflammation. Its active form, GLP-1(7-37), binds to the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R), but GLP-1 is rapidly degraded by dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) into GLP-1(9-37), which does not bind to the classical GLP-1R. Both peptides exhibit cardioprotective effects, although the underlying mechanisms are unclear and the role of GLP-1(9-37) remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated cardiac and metabolic effects of GLP-1(9-37) in a mouse model of cardiac pressure overload. LacZ and GLP-1(9-37) were overexpressed using an AAV vector system. While GLP-1(9-37) does not affect glucose metabolism, it mechanistically activates key metabolic regulators, as evidenced by increased AMPK and PGC1α signalling. This shift suggests an improvement in cellular energy balance and mitochondrial function under hypertrophic stress conditions. GLP-1(9-37) was also found to mitigate adverse cardiac remodelling. Treatment is associated with reduced septal thickness and decreased cardiac fibrosis, indicating attenuation of structural hypertrophy. In summary, our data suggest a protective role of GLP-1(9-37) in pressure-overload-induced cardiac remodelling, which is associated with AMPK/PGC1α-signalling.

title: Interpretation of non-statistically significant results in randomised controlled clinical trials in rehabilitation: a cross sectional analysis.
journal: The Journal of manual & manipulative therapy
abstract: To assess the prevalence of misinterpretation of non-statistically significant results, both in the abstract and in the article conclusions, in a sample of randomized controlled trials with non-statistically significant primary outcomes published in rehabilitation journals, and the reporting of the primary outcomes in accordance with the CONSORT Guidelines. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted of all RCTs with non-statistically significant primary outcomes in five general rehabilitation journals with the highest Impact Factor, published between 2019 and 2023. The objective of this analysis was to assess the prevalence of misinterpretation of non-statistically significant results, both in the abstract and in the article conclusions, in a sample of RCTs with non-statistically significant results and reporting of primary outcomes according to CONSORT guidelines. The analysis included 31 trials. The most common interpretation of non-statistically significant results was the evidence of absence, both in the abstract (74.2%) and the article (58.1%). Only four (12.9%) studies in the abstract and five (16.1%) conclusions in the article suggested the correct interpretation as the absence of evidence. Adherence to CONSORT guidelines was moderate, with only 61.3% of trials reporting results summaries for each arm, effect size, and confidence interval. There is a need for increased rigor in reporting and interpreting non-statistically significant results in rehabilitation trials. Evidence misinterpretations can adversely impact clinical decision-making and future research directions. Efforts should be made to promote accurate interpretation of statistical results, emphasize the importance of analyzing confidence intervals, and develop educational interventions to improve statistical literacy.

title: More Than the Visual Cortex, Age-Related Differences in Representational Momentum Stem From Network Reorganization: Insights From Dynamic Functional Connectivity.
abstract: When estimating the final location of moving targets, the individual's judgment tends to exhibit a systematic forward displacement along the direction of motion, a phenomenon termed representational momentum (RM). The age effect on RM has been a focus of research, and a recent study reports an age-related increase in forward displacement among older adults, potentially linked to functional decline in the visual cortex. However, this study exclusively focused on the visual cortex, thereby limiting a comprehensive understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying age-related differences in RM. To address this limitation, the neural basis of age-related differences in RM was investigated for the first time by combining resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging with whole-brain dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) analysis. The results revealed a significant increase in forward displacement among older adults compared with younger adults, particularly when targets moved from left to right. Neuroimaging data revealed reduced flexibility in transitioning between brain states and prolonged dwell time in the "weak state" characterized by weak and sparse connectivity, in older adults compared to younger adults. Moreover, within this "weak state," attenuated intranetwork connectivity and increased internetwork connectivity were observed in the aging brain. Critically, alterations in these dFC metrics partially mediated the relationship between age and forward displacement. These findings are discussed within the framework of computational theory and the dedifferentiation and compensation hypothesis of brain aging.

title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
abstract: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition. Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p < 0.001), as were length of stay (8 vs 5 days; p < 0.001), thromboembolic events (6.5% vs 1.8%; p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups. In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.

title: Perspectives on Brain Autopsy in Individuals With Intellectual Disabilities: A Qualitative Study With Dutch stakeholders.
journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
abstract: Brain autopsy has the potential to advance understanding of neurobiological and genetic mechanisms underlying intellectual disabilities (IDs), which may help improve health care and even inform therapies. However, for unknown reasons, it is rarely performed. This study aimed to explore attitudes and barriers toward clinical and scientific brain autopsy in people with ID. Four focus group discussions and six semi-structured interviews were conducted with Dutch adults with ID, parents and professionals. A total of 5 individuals with ID, 12 parents, 4 patient organization representatives and 13 professionals were interviewed. Most adults with ID and parents were not informed nor aware of brain autopsy but expressed willingness to contribute to research, particularly in rare genetic etiologies. Parents expressed most variance in attitudes and were more likely to consent to clinical than scientific brain autopsy, with emotional and ethical concerns as key barriers. Adults with ID emphasized respectful body return for a meaningful farewell. Professionals reported legal, organizational, financial and communicational barriers, with treating physicians reporting difficulties broaching this sensitive topic. Although attitudes toward brain autopsy were often positive and pragmatic, a variety of barriers were identified, of which some were unique to the ID community. Improving awareness, information, communication and organizational support may help overcome barriers.

title: Superficial facial musculature in naked mole-rats: Adaptations to a subterranean niche.
abstract: Naked mole-rats (Heterocephalus glaber) are eusocial rodents with unusually long lifespans. Adaptations to their subterranean habitat include large, well-innervated incisors used for digging underground tunnel systems; oral folds that close behind the incisors; and a specialized tactile system (sensitive incisors in addition to tactile hairs that cover the entire body). This well-developed tactile system compensates for their reduced visual and auditory systems. Naked mole-rats are functionally blind and have small eyes, even compared to other African mole-rat species. They also have relatively poor auditory capabilities as well as absent pinnae. Although few studies have characterized the facial musculature of naked mole-rats, their facial musculature would be expected to have evolved commensurately with adaptations to a subterranean niche. To examine this, we performed detailed dissections of superficial facial musculature in adult naked mole-rats. This included muscle identification and characterization of attachment sites compared to what has previously been shown in rats. Our dissections demonstrated reduced musculature associated with the eyes (e.g., orbicularis oculi), the ears (e.g., auricularis posterior and interscutularis muscles), and the dorsal head (frontalis and occipitalis muscles), but well-developed musculature facilitating movements of the nose and mouth, befitting the roles of these anatomical structures in sensory perception and social interactions. Our findings not only provide insights into the evolutionary adaptations of naked mole-rat facial musculature to a subterranean niche, but will also help inform future studies assessing and interpreting social-emotional communication in naked mole-rats through the lens of species-specific adaptations in the musculature underlying facial expressions.

title: Cortical Macro- and Microstructural Alterations in Multiple System Atrophy and Their Clinical Correlates.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is primarily characterized by subcortical neurodegeneration. However, neuropathological evidence indicates that cortical neurodegeneration is also part of the disease. Conventional neuroimaging measures, such as cortical thickness (CTh), have been used to assess cortical macrostructural alterations, but findings remain limited and inconclusive. In this context, cortical mean diffusivity (cMD) has emerged as a promising marker of microstructural integrity, capturing alterations beyond macrostructural changes in other neurodegenerative disorders. However, its role in MSA remains largely unexplored. The objective of the study was to characterize cortical macro- and microstructural alterations in MSA and assess associations with clinical severity and cognitive performance. T1-weighted and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), clinical, and neuropsychological assessments were obtained in 29 patients with MSA and 35 age- and sex-matched controls (HCs). Cortical macro- and microstructural alterations were evaluated using CTh and cMD, respectively. Group comparisons and correlations between MRI-derived cortical measures and clinical, cognitive, and neurodegeneration biomarkers were conducted (P < 0.05, false discovery rate [FDR]-corrected). Patients with MSA exhibited widespread increases in cMD, predominantly affecting the frontal and temporal cortices. This pattern partially overlapped with cortical thinning, although cMD alterations extended to rostral-lateral, rostral-medial, and inferior-medial regions. In MSA, increased cMD was associated with global cognitive impairment, whereas cortical thinning correlated with disease severity. MSA involves concurrent macro- and microstructural cortical alterations, with microstructural changes potentially preceding overt atrophy and indicating early pathology. Distinct cMD and CTh patterns suggest partially independent processes, whereas differential clinical associations highlight their complementarity. Together, these markers improve the characterization of cortical degeneration and disease heterogeneity. © 2026 The Author(s).
