title: [Acute neonatal effects following prenatal venlafaxine exposure].
abstract: Venlafaxine is a serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor. Intrauterine exposure may cause neonatal withdrawal symptoms known as poor neonatal adaptation syndrome (PNAS). In this case report, we present a term newborn with respiratory distress and neurological hyperexcitability after birth following maternal venlafaxine treatment. Evaluation excluded infectious and neurological causes, and symptoms resolved in days. PNAS should be considered despite early symptoms. Regional variation in observation practices may affect recognition of PNAS, underscoring the need for awareness of the condition.

title: [Alpha-gal allergy].
abstract: Alpha-gal allergy is a tick-borne allergy caused by IgE antibodies against the oligosaccharide alpha-gal. Alpha-gal is found in meat from mammals and in mammal-derived medications. The allergy often results in a delayed reaction 2-6 hours after ingestion. Symptoms commonly include urticaria and abdominal pain, but may progress to severe anaphylaxis, often influenced by cofactors such as exercise, alcohol, or NSAIDs. Diagnosis relies on patient history, as no laboratory test offers both high sensitivity and specificity. Treatment consists of avoidance strategies and the use of adrenaline autoinjectors, as argued in this review.

title: Small Molecule-Mediated Nrf2 Activation as a Neuroprotective Approach in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease resulting in progressive demyelination of the central nervous system, leading to symptoms such as motor discoordination, cognitive deficits, and ocular dysfunction. Oxidative stress is a crucial component in the pathogenesis of multiple sclerosis, with reactive oxygen species contributing to myelin destruction, neuronal injury, and disruption of the blood-brain barrier resulting in symptom progression. For this reason, reducing oxidative stress has gained attention as a promising mechanism of disease control. Nuclear factor erythroid-2-related factor-2 (Nrf2) is a master regulator of the cellular antioxidant and anti-inflammatory response throughout the body, including the central nervous system. Nrf2 functions as a transcription factor to activate the expression of genes involved in detoxification and antioxidant defense, thus playing a critical role in limiting neuronal oxidative damage resulting from multiple sclerosis. Since no curative treatments are currently available for multiple sclerosis, recognizing potential new drugs that target earlier stages of the disease may be a viable strategy to intervene in disease progression and improve quality of life for the patient. This review explores how Nrf2 is a promising target for intervention in multiple sclerosis and that many Nrf2 activators exhibit robust efficacy, highlighting their potential as novel agents for multiple sclerosis treatment.

title: Levodopa-Induced Slow Dystonic Dyskinesia in a Patient With Progressive Supranuclear Palsy-Corticobasal Syndrome.
MEC-BioSense: Material-Encoded Capillary Biointerface for Autonomous Whole-Blood Biomarker Sensing.
abstract: Bioelectronic sensing in complex biological fluids is often constrained not by molecular recognition, but by poor coordination of transport, separation, and interfacial interactions at the material level. Here, we present a material-encoded capillary biointerface that integrates microporous media, microfluidic geometry, and a hydrophilic graphene/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate)/Prussian Blue bioelectronic interface into a unified, self-regulated architecture. Capillary forces generated within a microfiber network are redistributed through vent-regulated pathways and stabilized at a hydrophilic mixed ionic-electronic interface, enabling controlled plasma extraction, transport, and analyte delivery without external actuation. System performance is governed by the balance between capillary driving pressure and distributed hydrodynamic resistance, defining an operating regime that simultaneously achieves >99% cellular exclusion, ∼80-93% protein recovery, and stable interfacial wetting. Within this regime, undiluted whole blood is autonomously converted into a reproducible electrochemical signal. Using glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) as a model biomarker, the platform enables direct sample-to-answer detection within ∼9 min, spanning 0.02 pg mL-1 to 200 ng mL-1 with an ultralow detection limit (∼0.01 fg mL-1) and reduced pre-analytical loss relative to centrifugation. These results establish that analytical performance is governed primarily by pre-analytical transport and interfacial regulation and introduce a generalizable nano/micro-engineered framework for autonomous, scalable point-of-care biointerfaces.

title: Tailoring Ion Exchange Efficiency in Synaptic Electrochemical Memtransistors Through Three-Dimensional Artificial Crystal Engineering.
abstract: Electronic synapses featuring conduction modulation for synaptic weight update play a central role in implementing neuromorphic computing. Though memristors and memtransistors operating via ion exchange for conductance modulation have demonstrated synaptic functionality, their planar architectures suffer from a reduced interfacial area during lateral scaling, limiting their dynamic range of conductance modulation. Here, an electrochemical memtransistor is presented that replaces conventional planar layout with a precisely engineered 3D structure composed of an SU-8 organic reservoir and ZnO channel, fabricated using proximity-field nanopatterning. This design increases the effective oxygen ion-exchange interfacial area available for conductance modulation without enlarging the device footprint. The 3D device achieves a dynamic range nearly 34-fold larger than a planar counterpart, withstands over 104 updating pulses, and exhibits key biological synaptic dynamics. Deep neural network simulations based on the measured weight-update characteristics show improved classification accuracy over the planar control, and the inherent fading memory of the device supports reservoir computing. These findings establish deterministic 3D structural engineering as a scalable strategy for decoupling device footprint from synaptic modulation capability, thereby addressing a scaling bottleneck in neuromorphic hardware.

title: Flexible Ultralow-Power IGZO Multimodal Synaptic Transistors for Thermally Robust Neuromorphic Vision and Wearable Heatstroke Monitoring.
abstract: Multimodal synaptic devices are increasingly required to enable more reliable and informed decision-making in next-generation neuromorphic systems. A wafer-scale, energy-efficient flexible optoelectronic synaptic transistor based on an a-IGZO channel and ALD-deposited HfO2 gate dielectric is demonstrated. The device is fabricated on a rigid silicon substrate and subsequently transformed into a flexible form, maintaining stable electrical characteristics under repeated bending (radius ∼3 cm). The device enables multimodal sensing by responding to optical stimulus and a wide temperature range (10-75°C), capturing signals such as body temperature, ambient conditions, and sunlight. Under optical stimulation, the transistor emulates key synaptic functions, including EPSC, PPF, and the transition from STM to LTM, as well as learning-forgetting-relearning behavior. Reliable synaptic responses are achieved at a low drain voltage of 0.01 V, with an energy consumption of 1.6 fJ per synaptic event. The behavior is governed by defect-mediated carrier trapping and detrapping in IGZO. System-level applications include heatstroke risk classification (99.6% accuracy, within the physiological temperature range 37°C-42°C) and neuromorphic vision sensing enabled by persistent photoconductivity. These multimodal capabilities enable both heatstroke monitoring and thermally robust vision processing within a unified platform. The results present a scalable platform for low-power neuromorphic and wearable healthcare applications.

title: Heterogeneous Negative Gray Matter Volume Deviations Converge on a Shared Depression Circuit Associated With Symptoms and rTMS Response.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by marked heterogeneity in regional negative gray matter volume (GMV) deviations, obscuring the network basis of the disorder. Here, subject-specific normative GMV deviation maps are integrated with the human connectome using atrophy network mapping. Extreme negative GMV deviations in a medication-naive, first-episode MDD discovery cohort (n = 105) and an independent multisite validation cohort (n = 1265) converge on a reproducible depression circuit characterized by positive connectivity with subcortical-limbic regions and negative connectivity with frontoparietal and default mode network hubs. Circuit coupling tracks depressive symptom severity, follows gradients of depression-risk gene expression, and shows preliminary translational relevance: stronger negative connectivity at individualized rTMS targets is associated with greater clinical improvement. These findings reconcile heterogeneous structural deviations with the shared MDD phenotype and may inform future circuit-based neuromodulation studies.

title: CRH-CRHR1 Signaling in BNST-vHPC Projections Mediates Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain-Induced Anxiety- and Depression-Like Behaviors.
abstract: Chronic pain is frequently accompanied by anxiety and depression, but the mechanisms linking nociceptive sensitization to affective dysfunction remain unclear. In a mouse model of chronic constriction injury of the infraorbital nerve (CION), we identified a corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-dependent circuit through which trigeminal neuropathic pain promotes anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. CION induces hyperactivity of the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST) neurons, particularly CRH-expressing neurons. Chemogenetic inhibition of BNST or BNSTCRH neurons alleviates CION-induced mechanical allodynia and improves anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. These effects are accompanied by increased Crh expression in the BNST, and local Crh deletion attenuates the behavioral abnormalities. BNSTCRH neurons directly innervate the ventral hippocampus (vHPC), where terminal inhibition reduces allodynia and affective deficits in CION mice. Postsynaptically, chronic pain shifts the functional output of this projection toward excitation. vHPC target neurons express Crhr1, and CRHR1 blockade prevents BNSTCRH terminal stimulation-induced excitation, reduces pathway-driven behavioral deficits, and ameliorates CION-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. Conversely, intra-vHPC CRH infusion in naïve mice induces anxiety- and depression-like behaviors similar to those observed after CION. Together, these findings establish a BNSTCRH-vHPC CRH-CRHR1 circuit linking trigeminal neuropathic pain to affective comorbidity and identify CRH-CRHR1 signaling as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: A Case Report of a Rare Subserous Uterine Adenomyoma Mimicking an Ovarian Cyst With Literature Review.
journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research
abstract: The uterine corpus adenomyoma is a benign mixed epithelial and mesenchymal tumor, classified by the World Health Organization, fifth edition (2020), as a distinct lesion composed of endometrioid-type glands, endometrioid-type stroma, and smooth muscle. Subserosal adenomyomas with a pedunculated polypoid configuration represent a rare morphological presentation. We describe the case of a 46-year-old woman who presented for surgical evaluation of a right ovarian mass. Preoperative investigations, including transvaginal pelvic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), showed a right adnexal cystic lesion. The patient underwent robot-assisted laparoscopy that suggested a subserosal cystic adenomyoma of the posterior uterine wall, a diagnosis confirmed by histological examination. This case underscores the importance of detailed intraoperative and pathological assessment for diagnosing pedunculated subserosal adenomyoma, which may be misdiagnosed clinically or radiologically. In similar situations, it is essential to consider the possibility of a subserosal adenomyoma to ensure appropriate preoperative counseling for the patient.

title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: A Review in Neuroimaging.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. Automated segmentation and volumetric analysis improve reproducibility, speed, and standardization of tumor quantification and response assessment. In research, large language and multimodal models extract structured information from radiology reports and medical records. Collaborative initiatives, such as BraTS and FeTS, have established standardized, privacy-compliant frameworks for large-scale quantitative analyses. Tumor-specific applications include noninvasive molecular profiling in gliomas, grading and recurrence prediction in meningiomas, detection and response assessment in brain metastases, and pediatric-specific modeling aligned with RAPNO. However, AI models remain sensitive to technical and biological variations across institutions, limiting their clinical utility unless appropriate training and validation is performed. Nevertheless, progress is evident in prospective, biopsy-validated infiltration mapping, assessment of resection extent aligned with RANO-Resect, and standardization through AI-RANO. Emerging directions include foundation models, uncertainty estimation, federated learning, AI-enhanced ultra-low-field MRI, and dual-tracer PET. When used as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for the imaging team, AI can increasingly improve the utility, reproducibility, and efficiency of quantitative, multiparametric imaging in patients with brain tumors.

title: When Fluctuating Ptosis and Diplopia Are Not Myasthenia Gravis: A Case of Eosinophilic Orbital Myositis Treated With IL-5 Inhibition.
Spinal Cord-Computer Interface for Motor Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury: Conceptual Framework, Mechanisms, and Clinical Translation.
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) remains a clinically challenging condition characterized by profound functional deficits. For decades, traditional therapeutic strategies prioritizing structural repair, including axonal regeneration and biological scaffolds, have largely failed to yield significant functional recovery. This stagnation has catalyzed a paradigm shift driven by the convergence of neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and bioelectronic engineering, leading to the emergence of the spinal cord-computer interface (SCCI). Unlike brain-computer interfaces that typically bypass the body to control external devices, SCCI functions as an input-based neural engineering technology designed to directly engage dormant yet anatomically intact neural circuits situated below the lesion. By delivering precise, programmable spatiotemporal epidural electrical stimulation, SCCI reactivates specific spinal motor circuitry to enable the restoration of voluntary motor control in previously paralyzed limbs. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of SCCI by tracing its conceptual evolution from early gate control theory to modern neuromodulation paradigms. We dissect the underlying physiological mechanisms and integrate global research findings to highlight how rapid technological advancements and clinical breakthroughs are reshaping the landscape of motor rehabilitation, ultimately offering a viable therapeutic pathway for patients worldwide.

title: Donor-Site Morbidity After Buccinator Myomucosal Flap: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract: Buccinator myomucosal flaps (BMF) are increasingly used for reconstruction of small- to medium-sized intraoral defects because they replace oral mucosa with similar tissue. However, donor-site morbidity and its determinants remain poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate donor-site morbidity after BMF harvest and identify factors associated with unfavorable outcomes. A retrospective international multicenter cohort study was conducted across 11 centers (10 in Europe and one in India). Adult patients undergoing reconstruction with BMF after oncologic resection and a minimum follow-up of 6 months were included. Donor-site morbidity was assessed during dedicated follow-up visits using a standardized clinical scoring system evaluating mouth opening, oral commissure symmetry, vestibular restoration, cheek lining reconstruction, and cosmetic outcome. A total of 340 patients were included (mean age 58.6 ± 13.9 years; 50% female; mean flap area 14.6 ± 6.2 cm2). The mean donor-site outcome score was 10.7 ± 3.4. At multivariable linear mixed-effects analysis accounting for center, adjuvant radiotherapy or radiochemotherapy and donor-site closure by secondary healing were independently associated with lower scores, whereas the buccal artery myomucosal island flap and the tunnelized facial artery myomucosal island flap were associated with higher scores. Wound dehiscence was the most frequent complication (9.1%). In 223 patients with available data, higher adherence to rehabilitation exercises was associated with improved outcome scores, both with and without adjuvant radiotherapy. BMF provides reliable reconstruction with generally favorable donor-site outcomes. Morbidity is mainly influenced by adjuvant radiotherapy, donor-site management, flap design, and adherence to postoperative rehabilitation exercises.

title: Unlocking Green Coffee Secrets: Classical and Non-Destructive Prediction of Chemical Composition.
abstract: The quality of green coffee is influenced by a number of chemical properties, of which caffeine, chlorogenic acids, and pH play a prominent role. The type of coffee, the processing method, and the place of origin can also play a role in the variation of these parameters. The aim of the study was to develop methods based on NIR spectroscopy and chemometric tools to predict the pH, caffeine content, and chlorogenic acid composition of green coffee samples. As a result of this research, a successful method development was carried out by chemometric analysis of data obtained by Fourier transform near-infrared spectroscopy (FT-NIRS) and instrumental analytical methods. The pH, caffeine content, and the amount of the major chlorogenic acids of green coffee were investigated. Different data processing and variable selection methods were applied to improve the performance of the mathematical models. Of these, in all cases orthogonal signal correction (OSC) proved to be the most effective. These findings demonstrate the potential of FT-NIRS combined with chemometric modelling as a rapid, non-destructive, and sustainable approach for the simultaneous assessment of key chemical quality parameters in green coffee. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: A rapid, non-destructive, and sustainable method for predicting quality traits of green coffees-such as pH, caffeine, and major chlorogenic acids-using FT-NIR spectroscopy combined with chemometrics is provided. This enables faster, cheaper, and more efficient quality control across the coffee supply chain, from producers to industry and on. The built models support authentication, processing optimization, and future monitoring of roasted or brewed coffees.

title: Bridging Inpatient and Community Care Following First Episode Psychosis: A Pilot Feasibility and Acceptability Study of a Brief Psychological Intervention.
abstract: This study evaluated the implementation feasibility and acceptability of a brief CBT-informed psychological intervention designed to bridge inpatient and community care for young adults experiencing a first episode of psychosis (FEP). A six-session individual CBT-informed intervention was delivered to patients experiencing a FEP approaching discharge from a specialist early intervention inpatient unit. The intervention commenced on the ward (the initial session) and continued into the community. Feasibility was assessed from a service implementation perspective, including recruitment, uptake, retention, intervention completion, and outcome measure completion rates. Acceptability was evaluated using satisfaction ratings and qualitative interviews. During a seven-month period, 43 patients were screened, and 38 were eligible to participate. Twenty-eight (74%) consented, six (15%) disengaged, and 17 (44%) completed all six sessions and study measures. Findings indicated that the intervention could be successfully delivered across inpatient and community settings within routine clinical care. Patients reported high satisfaction with therapy (mean satisfaction score = 4.76/5). Qualitative feedback highlighted the value of psychological continuity across care settings, development of coping strategies, and opportunities to make sense of admission and recovery experiences. Clinical outcome measures were successfully collected; however, the study was not designed to evaluate intervention effectiveness. Findings suggest that delivering a brief CBT-informed intervention across inpatient and community services is feasible within routine clinical practice and acceptable to young adults experiencing FEP. Further controlled research is required to evaluate clinical effectiveness and longer-term outcomes.

title: [Research progress on genome-wide association study of circadian chronotype in adolescents].
journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]
abstract: Circadian chronotype refers to stable individual differences in sleep-wake cycles and activity timing preferences, and is closely associated with sleep patterns, behavioral characteristics, and mental health. In recent years, with the rapid development of genome-wide association studies (GWAS), increasing attention has been paid to the genetic basis of chronotype. Previous studies have demonstrated that chronotype is highly heritable, and GWAS have identified multiple genetic variants associated with chronotype in adult populations, involving core circadian clock genes, neurotransmitter signaling pathways, and protein degradation regulatory pathways. However, adolescence represents a critical period of circadian development and sleep pattern transition, and the genetic regulation and health implications of chronotype in adolescents remain insufficiently understood. Evening chronotype and delayed circadian timing have been closely associated with insufficient sleep, depression, anxiety, attention deficits, and other mental health problems among adolescents. This review summarizes recent advances in GWAS of chronotype, focusing on its genetic architecture, potential regulatory mechanisms, and current evidence in adolescent populations. Furthermore, the associations between chronotype, sleep characteristics, and mental health outcomes are discussed, providing theoretical insights into the genetic mechanisms underlying adolescent circadian changes and their health implications, and supporting the development of individualized prevention and intervention strategies.
